title: ResultEnvelope
description: The standard output envelope, emitted when an invocation's effective output kind is `RESULT_ENVELOPE` and by every `apply` op. Resolve the effective kind from the invocation's matching profile: a matching `operationalProfiles[].returns.views[]` overrides `operationalProfiles[].returns.kind`, that profile's primary kind; `RAW_JSON`, `RAW_TEXT`, `EMPTY_STDOUT` and `NDJSON_STREAM` (an artifact or catalog value, a rendered view, no stdout, a newline-delimited stream of protocol frames) are not this schema. THREE ORTHOGONAL AXES, never conflated: `ok`, the operation succeeded; `valid`, a kernel-validity VERDICT, present only where a gate produced one; `verification`/`engine`, who vouches for it. So a read that succeeded is `ok:true` with NO `valid`, because it established no verdict. Optional keys are omitted when not applicable, and which appear follows what the invocation actually did, never the verb. TWO KINDS OF ADDRESS, and a coordinate-free one is NOT a declaration: a model-ELEMENT path (a declaration, such as `diagnostics[].where.path`, `where.rule` or a runtime payload's `declaration`) always has a LEADING SLASH, while a document CELL address is A12's canonical instance pointer, with NO leading slash and `[1]` omitted, so a runtime `field` `Order/Lines/LineTotal` names repetition 1 of every level, spelled like the declaration it is not. A runtime key's `format` names its contract: `a12-pointer` is always canonical; `a12-message-address` is canonical exactly when it names ONE cell, else the interpreter's house form with a leading slash and every index (`/Order[1]/Lines[0]/LineTotal`), since A12 defines no pointer string for a wildcard or unresolved level. That is decided PER ADDRESS, not per key, so one message legitimately shows both spellings, a one-row `field` beside a whole-column `referenced` operand. Test the leading slash to tell them apart; the per-key contracts are in `schema model eval` / `schema model compute` / `schema rule eval`.

target.description: the element family acted on: model | rule | computation | field | group | typedef | include | config | workspace | patterns | profile | where-used | meta

op.description: the operation: add | read | modify | remove | validate | check | explain | describe | export | eval | compute | compare | scaffold | …

outcome.description: The execution result class. `error`: the tool itself failed (an unexpected throwable, exit 70), unlike `rejected` (input rejected, exit 1). `read` covers EVERY non-mutating class (a query, verdict, runtime observation or comparison), so `outcome` alone does not tell you whether `valid` may be present. For `batch`, `completed` means every child was dispatched: inspect `data.allExitedZero` and each child's exit. An ordinary batch with a nonzero child sets outer `ok` false and exits 1; an observation batch (`batch --observations`) sets `ok` true and exits 0 after full dispatch and the artifact write, whatever `allExitedZero` says. Batch is non-transactional, so an earlier successful write remains, unlike `apply`, whose ops are one transaction and roll back together

ok.description: The operation succeeded: true for applied | preview | read | staged; false for refused | rejected | error. A completed ordinary batch is true only when `data.allExitedZero` is; a completed observation batch is true when every child was dispatched and the artifact was written, whatever `data.allExitedZero` says, and false when the artifact write failed

valid.description: The subject model is kernel-valid, a consistency VERDICT distinct from `ok`. PRESENT only on a genuine verdict (`model check`, `rule check`, `workspace check`, a `patterns` scaffold review) and on a rejection the kernel gate produced (then `false`); ABSENT on every read, runtime evaluation, comparison, mutation, refusal and pre-flight rejection. A per-entry `valid` inside `data` (`workspace list --validate`, `workspace check`) is a different, model-scoped fact that never affects the exit code. THE ABSENCE IS ASYMMETRIC, the one trap here: a gate that REJECTED emits `valid:false`, a gate that ACCEPTED emits nothing, so absence covers both 'no verdict' and 'a green verdict'. Never read it as 'nothing was checked': `verification` answers that. An accepted `--dry-run` preview is this case: `ok:true`, `verification:KERNEL_CONFIRMED` and no `valid` mean the kernel DID arbitrate and passed the change

verification.description: How a consistency gate arbitrated THIS invocation. KERNEL_CONFIRMED: a kernel backend ran the gate (the CLI always bundles one). STRUCTURAL_ONLY: the gate ran with NO backend, so a verdict beside it reflects structural prechecks only and must not be read as kernel-green (a library-consumer posture). PORTABLE_CHECKED: the EXPLICITLY REQUESTED kernel-free checker arbitrated (`model check --engine=portable`), a real re-implementation of A12 constraints rather than a precheck, and never a kernel confirmation. PORTABLE_CHECKED says nothing about COMPLETENESS: that checker cannot report a model VALID today, so a model it finds nothing wrong with returns NO `valid` key at exit 3, and its coverage evidence (`data.status`, `data.complete`, `data.gaps`) is the half to read. PRESENT whenever the gate ran, a `rejected` run included (KERNEL_CONFIRMED means the kernel ARBITRATED, not that the model was valid) and a WRITE included, since an edit verb gates before writing; ABSENT when no gate ran. So it is per-INVOCATION, never per-verb: `model report` carries it and `model report --tree` does not, `field add` does and `model normalize` (a pure reformat) does not. On a `--dry-run` preview it answers what `written:false` cannot: nothing was written, but the change WAS checked

engine.description: (runtime evaluation only) which implementation produced the semantic observation. `model eval`/`model compute`/`rule eval` evaluate through the kernel-free DM_INTERPRETER. Orthogonal to `verification`: an evaluation yields observations, not a verdict, so a runtime envelope carries `engine` and never `valid`

engineRequested.description: (a verdict from a verb that SELECTS an engine, today `model check`) the engine the caller asked for, present for all three request shapes, the default included, since an absent `--engine` IS a request for the kernel. The option spells them `kernel` and `portable`; the envelope uses the runtime `engine` key's names instead, so one reader learns one set of engine names. ABSENT on a verdict from a verb with no choice (`rule check`, `workspace check`), where `verification` still names what arbitrated

engineExecuted.description: (with `engineRequested`) the engine that actually produced the verdict, derived from the arbitration receipt so it cannot contradict `verification`. It ALWAYS EQUALS `engineRequested`: the selected engine is never substituted, not on an incomplete answer, a failure, or when the other engine would agree, and no envelope is emitted where they would differ. Published so a consumer can assert this rather than trust it

engineVersion.description: The build of the engine that produced this result, read from that engine, not stated by dmtool. With `engine` (a runtime observation): the `:interpreter` release for DM_INTERPRETER, the kernel actually on the classpath (never the built-against pin) for A12_KERNEL. With `engineExecuted` (a verdict): the portable checker artifact's own baked version, so a tool linked against another checker reports that one, or the live-classpath kernel version for A12_KERNEL. A verdict and an observation never share an envelope, so the key has one meaning wherever it appears

toolVersion.description: (with `engine`) the `dmtool` build that projected and serialized the observation. Emitted beside `engineVersion`, not inferred from it: evaluation semantics can move in the engine while pointer spelling, summaries and envelope shape move independently in the tool, so one version cannot identify what produced a retained result

summary.description: one human-readable line (the agent's quick read / log line)

changed.description: (mutations) the delta on success — e.g. {added, kind}, a refactor's rewritten references

data.description: (reads/queries/verdicts/comparisons) the op's payload — explanation tree, model card, fired-list, per-model verdicts, a profile comparison, …; shape is op-specific (see `schema <target> <op>`)

diagnostics.description: Structured findings (see `schema diagnostic`). NOT A DEFECT COUNT, in either direction: a rule with two independent defects can return ONE diagnostic (the gate suppresses the other), and one defect can return TWO (the same problem under two `MVK_*` codes). Which objection wins is not a fixed order, measured both ways. So read a lone diagnostic as AN objection, never THE objection: to attribute a refusal to one gate, remove the other candidate defect and re-run. A precheck refusal (`RK_*`, `source: PRECHECK`) means the kernel gate was never asked, so no `MVK_*` appears beside it however many kernel-level defects the input carries.

written.description: whether this invocation wrote its selected model or artifact destination to disk

output.description: the path of the model or artifact destination written by this invocation; absent when `written:false`

diagnostics.summary: /Order/DeliveryDate is referenced by 1 element(s); removing it would dangle them
diagnostics.fix: pass --cascade to remove the referrers too, or remove them first

diagnostics.summary: At 'Abs'It is not allowed to use constants.
diagnostics.fix: wrap a field or an expression, not an immediate literal
